claims.explanation: GW-843682X is annotated as a PLK inhibitor, but its transcriptional signature closely matches tubulin/microtubule inhibitors, suggesting it may act as a microtubule poison. Sensitivity is strongly associated with TP53 mutation and co-occurring alterations in RAS/RTK/MAPK pathway genes (KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, MET, ERBB3, NF1), which may impair mitotic checkpoint and apoptosis, leading to selective killing of these lines.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines and may impair mitotic checkpoint/apoptosis
KRAS mutations are common in sensitive lines and may cooperate with mitotic stress
NRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may activate MAPK signaling
HRAS mutations observed in sensitive lines, potentially enhancing mitotic vulnerability
BRAF mutations in sensitive thyroid and endometrial lines, may activate MAPK
MET mutations in sensitive gastric and thyroid lines, may drive RTK signaling
ERBB3 mutations in sensitive lung lines, may contribute to RTK pathway activation
NF1 mutation in a sensitive rhabdomyosarcoma line, may hyperactivate RAS/MAPK
SMARCA4 mutations appear in several sensitive lines, may alter chromatin and mitotic regulation
CDKN2A deletions/mutations common in sensitive lines, may impair cell cycle checkpoints
STK11 mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but some resistant lines carry STK11 mutations, suggesting possible context-dependent protection
PTEN mutations are more frequent in resistant lines, possibly through PI3K/AKT-mediated survival
